summary: All request logic lives in one module, src/requests.py, with no persistence or external integration.
Tests cover approving a pending request, self-approval and approving a rejected request; the finance limit and the rejection path have no direct test.
An approver can approve a pending request.
An approver can reject a pending request.
Notifying the requester of a rejection is not implemented; a TODO marks it.
A requester cannot approve their own request.
Requests above the approval limit need an approver whose address ends in @finance; the code sets the limit at 5000, the README at 10 000.
Only a pending request can be approved or rejected.
reject() does not check who rejects: a requester can reject their own request.
The request logic and its tests are Python using only the standard library (unittest for the tests); no third-party package is imported.
The repository declares no Python version, entry point or deployment configuration and nothing was executed, so the callers, the runtime version and any deployed environment or revision are unknown.
The README declares the product's purpose and users: employees raise purchase requests, a manager approves or rejects them, and finance approves requests above 10 000.
No source states the product's business objectives, expected value or success measures; the repository has no analytics, metrics or roadmap.

The README calls the approver a manager, but approve() checks no role and accepts any approver other than the requester up to the limit; whether only managers may approve depends on callers outside the repository.
